old: For the billing service, invoices for nonprofit customers may be generated on the 5th of the month rather than the 1st.
new: All invoices should be generated on the 1st of each month. This keeps the billing schedule consistent across customer segments.
note: The general billing schedule does not cancel the documented nonprofit exception unless it explicitly addresses that exception. [relabelled 2026-09-27: NEW addresses the exception directly: 'All invoices', 'consistent across customer segments']

old: During the mobile-app launch, the payments team may deploy its API on Fridays if a production fix is required.
new: Production deployments are limited to Monday through Thursday so the support team has coverage for release issues.
note: The general deployment rule and the launch-specific payments exception can both be true if the exception remains scoped to the launch. [relabelled 2026-09-27: NEW conflicts with the launch exception but never addresses it; could be a restatement]

old: All production database migrations require approval from the database team.
new: The analytics team may run migrations on its staging database without database-team approval.
note: The later decision defines a staging-specific exception and does not conflict with the production migration requirement.

old: Support tickets marked urgent must receive a response within four hours.
new: Tickets assigned to the enterprise support team must receive a response within one business hour.
note: The enterprise rule applies to a subset of tickets while the urgent-ticket rule can continue to govern other urgent cases.

old: The payments team stores production secrets in AWS Secrets Manager.
new: The payments team's staging environment stores secrets in Azure Key Vault.
note: The decisions concern different environments, so there is no contradiction even though both discuss payments secrets.

old: The customer-success team holds its weekly planning meeting on Tuesday at 10:00 UTC.
new: The engineering team holds its weekly planning meeting on Tuesday at 10:00 UTC.
note: The same time and meeting cadence do not make the decisions equivalent because they concern different teams.

old: We will use PostgreSQL for the order-service database.
new: We will use PostgreSQL for the order-service database. The decision is owned by the platform team because they maintain the production cluster.
note: The core decision is unchanged; the later text only adds ownership information.

old: The product review is scheduled for Wednesday at 15:00 UTC.
new: The product review is scheduled for Wednesday at 15:00 UTC because the design team needs the morning for user interviews.
note: The meeting time remains identical and the later decision only supplies a reason.

old: We will keep the feature flag enabled for the beta cohort.
new: We will keep the feature flag enabled for the beta cohort through Friday, with Priya owning the rollout.
note: The later decision preserves the same flag choice and adds a duration and owner rather than changing the decision. [relabelled 2026-09-27: 'through Friday' adds an end date; NEW contains everything OLD said]

old: The release checklist requires security review, QA approval, and a product sign-off.
new: The release checklist requires security review, QA approval, and an engineering sign-off.
note: Two checklist requirements remain identical while the required approver for the third requirement is different.

old: The support workflow sends email alerts for high-priority tickets and assigns them to the on-call engineer.
new: The support workflow sends email alerts for high-priority tickets and assigns them to the customer-support lead.
note: The same workflow has two parts, and the assignment responsibility has a different answer while the alert behavior stays intact.

old: The onboarding process includes a security-training module, manager approval, and a laptop request.
new: The onboarding process includes a security-training module, manager approval, and an access-badge request.
note: The process has three parts and only the final requested item has a different answer.

old: Customer invoices are generated on the first business day of each month.
new: For the September launch campaign, customer invoices will be generated on September 18.
note: The later decision is explicitly limited to a single campaign period and can coexist with the permanent invoicing rule.

old: Production releases are permitted on weekdays after the release manager approves them.
new: For this week's launch, the release team will deploy on Saturday at 09:00 UTC because the customer has requested a weekend rollout.
note: The Saturday deployment is a temporary launch-specific arrangement and does not establish a different permanent release policy.

old: The weekly engineering review is held on Thursday at 16:00 UTC.
new: The weekly engineering review is held on Monday at 16:00 UTC.
note: Both statements govern the same recurring meeting and provide different regular meeting times.

old: The recommendation service uses Redis for its feature cache.
new: The recommendation service uses Memcached for its feature cache.
note: Both decisions answer the same infrastructure question for the same service, with different cache technologies.

old: The design team uses Figma for product mockups.
new: The design team uses Figma for product mockups, while the research team uses FigJam for workshop boards.
note: The original Figma decision remains intact and the later statement adds a separate tool choice for another activity. [relabelled 2026-09-27: NEW adds a separate research-team decision]

old: All customer data must be encrypted at rest.
new: Customer data in the internal analytics warehouse is exempt from encryption at rest because it contains only aggregated metrics.
note: One reading treats the warehouse statement as a scoped exception to the general rule; another treats it as a conflicting policy that should supersede the broad requirement for that data.

old: The mobile application sends crash reports to Sentry.
new: The mobile application sends crash reports to Sentry for production builds; debug builds send them to the internal logging service.
note: It can be read as preserving the original production decision while adding a debug case, or as defining the complete rule and narrowing the original statement's scope.

old: The support team will respond to priority-two tickets within eight business hours.
new: Priority-two tickets for customers in the enterprise plan receive a response within four business hours.
note: The later rule can be a narrower service-level exception for enterprise customers, but it could also be interpreted as the applicable response target for that subset and therefore replacing the broader target.
